scope: Resolve the four suites saved in audit/paused-native-port-2026-11-05.json; no live credentials or user files.
changes: Attachment assertions compare every original captured metadata field exactly after separating versioned display metadata. Display IDs/parts/attachments are independently verified; all four actual wire requests exclude UI metadata and display IDs.
The runtime attachment fixture retains exact reference/hash/metadata equality and checks display metadata without allowing original attachment bytes into saved history.
Composer test verifies the source max-h-64 (256px) cap, scale-adjusted cap, overflow scrolling, and shrink/reset to zero scroll range.

Windows editor regression holds an external non-delete-sharing read handle over the same UTF16 LE+BOM+LF kind of file. Normal and explicit-overwrite saves both fail safely, preserve exact file bytes and dirty buffer, leave no temporary file, then succeed after handle release.

validation.controlledFailure: Both new Windows rows report: Save failed; the previous file was preserved: Access is denied.

limits: The original full-suite editor denial did not recur; its actual external cause remains unresolved. Controlled sharing denial demonstrates expected failure semantics, not proof that the old failure was caused by a reader or antivirus.
No speculative retry, permission bypass, direct-write fallback or production save change was introduced.

An initial reproduction launch requested an offscreen plugin absent from the original editor target. GDB identified init_platform waiting in a modal error; only the owned process was stopped, then native-Windows hidden-process runs were used. This was a harness setup error, not an editor regression.

A dangling QJsonValueRef was caught in the newly added retained-history assertion during the first targeted rerun and corrected to an owning QJsonValue before the final pass; no engine change was needed.
These are focused suites, not a new full application integration result or complete parity claim.
